name: hyperframes-cli
description: Scaffold, inspect, preview and render HyperFrames projects; use local or explicitly authorized hosted workflows.

findings.excerpt: Run `npx hyperframes <command>` unless the project gives a wrapper; then use the wrapper. It needs Node.js 22+ and FFmpeg. Every command has `--help`; most take
1. Write, then `npx hyperframes lint` after the first pass and after structural changes.
2. `npx hyperframes check --json` and fix every error. While a lint error remains the layout and contrast audits don't run; "0 samples" means nothing was checke
3. `npx hyperframes snapshot` and read the PNGs (under `.hyperframes/artifacts/snapshots/`): that is how you see the video. With sub-compositions, snapshot a mi
4. `npx hyperframes preview --background`, check the URL answers 200, give the person the project URL and wait, unless they asked for the file or for no stops.
5. Time to render (step 4): `npx hyperframes render --quality looks -o out.mp4` (`draft` while iterating, `delivery` for the final; paid plan: `cloud render --f
"This element" or the current selection: `npx hyperframes preview --context --json --context-fields selection`; `no-selection` means ask them to click it.
Every write is kept and can be undone. At the start of a turn, `npx hyperframes history begin --who <you> --label "<plan>"`, then `history --since mine --who <y

If the track has no steady beat, the command fails and writes nothing. If ffmpeg is missing, run `npx hyperframes doctor`.
